summary: Use math to make sense of everyday things, like sorting snacks by color and counting each group.
Use math words like more, less and same, and know numbers can be shown with fingers, dice or numerals.
Notice math problems in daily life, like sharing crackers, and try out ways to solve them.
Count objects one by one to see how many, and count back from 5 for fun, like a rocket launch.
See how many are in a small group at a glance, without counting each one.
Compare groups to find which has more, and put groups together or take some away.
Split a small group, up to 4, into two parts in different ways and say how many in each.
Use position words like in front of, behind, left and right to say where things are.
Match and name flat and solid shapes of any size or turn, and build or draw with them.
Split a whole, like a cookie or a pile of crackers, into two equal halves or fair shares.
Copy, continue and make repeating patterns, like AB and ABC, with shapes or colors.
Put things in order by one feature, such as lining up blocks from longest to shortest.
Notice that things can be measured, such as how long, how heavy or how much they hold.
Compare things and describe them with measuring words like longer, bigger and lighter.
Measure with hands, footsteps or blocks, and try real tools like a tape measure or balance.
Say how things are alike and different, and keep count of answers with marks or a chart.
Sort things into groups by what they have in common, like color, pattern or shape.
